1.explanation: This snippet creates a fake Chrome trace with both Google-ad-injected user timings (ad_* and goog_*) and your own custom marks/measures. It then feeds that trace into the Lighthouse “user-timings” audit. By inspecting the output, you’ll see that the audit includes every single event—including the irrelevant ad/goog ones—thus reproducing the cluttering issue seen in the screenshot.
1.bug_scenario: When running the Lighthouse “user-timings” audit against pages that load Google Ads, those ad-injected marks and measures (e.g. “ad_slots_defined”, “goog_123_3_1_start”/“end”, etc.) all show up in the report and massively clutter the “User Timing marks and measures” section, as in the screenshot.
